name: code-corpus
title: Code corpus — semantic code retrieval alongside the memory bank (code-daemon-embed-v1)

ownerGateReview.note: Plan §7 records 14 join dispositions (lane conflicts resolved) and §9 lists 9 owner open questions, most resolved away-mode in §12.4. Still open at this feature's authoring: OQ5 (eval-set repo approval) and the champion-model default flip (owner decides from the WP8 report, never this feature).

cards.ruling: docs/features/code-corpus/code-corpus.feature + sibling spec.json per docs/features/README.md — NOT the legacy docs/work/features-* layout the QA catalog originally referenced (repointed by this task).

Keys are 'results' (existing) and 'code' (new). kind=memory serializes the exact legacy envelope with NO 'code' key at all (WhenWritingNull); kind=code/both always carry both keys, even when a section is empty (review F-02/03/12/13).

gitignore subset: '*' (one segment), '**' (zero-or-more segments as a whole segment), trailing '/' directory patterns, leading/anchored '/'; NO '!' negation in v1 (additive later); any-match-wins; case per host OS.

The watch whose scope contains the other wins. A broader add prunes every contained watch (entries stay; fingerprints cascade-deleted; new watch full-catches-up). A narrower add inside an existing watch is REJECTED with the covering watch named, not silently absorbed. Equal-path re-add is an idempotent no-op.

Always-ingest: code files are chunked (bundled counting tokenizer) and stored pending regardless of engine configuration. kind=code degrades to FTS5-only with a warning. A configured-but-unloadable engine (bad manifest/dims) is the only case that refuses code search outright — memory is never affected either way.

Refused at 'model set code local' configure time — vec_code is a fixed float[768] index with no dimension-reconcile phase (unlike the memory bank), so this is the only gate. D3 dimension-reconcile machinery is documented as an extension point, not exercised in v1.

Code never syncs. StripNonSyncableAsync DROPs code_entries/code_fts/vec_code (and shadow tables) from every pushed snapshot, on all push paths (local, merged, retry-merged). Pull/merge never name the code tables.

NOT the model_migration outbox (single-row, hard-coded memory relay query, ToolGate closes all tools — three disqualifying facts). Instead: 'model set code local' invalidates pending code rows in the SAME transaction as the settings write; a separate code-reindex maintenance job drains them; no ToolGate interaction, so memory tools are never blocked.

ADR-0094 reverses the v1 exclusion: every kind records via RecordSearchSafeAsync (memory as before, both with the memory leg's count and files, code with the code count and an empty file list). Code paths never enter the table (rows sync off-machine; ADR-0085 never-syncs rule). Performance metrics still record for kind=both's memory leg, with the query hash omitted rather than the whole row (integration review S6, unchanged). The envelope always carries Meta.CorrelationId.
Returns an empty code section, documented in the tool description — not a refusal. Code is always project-scoped.

in: A second, code-only corpus in the same memory.db: code_entries + code_fts (FTS5) + vec_code (vec0, float[768], distance_metric=cosine)
memory_search gains kind: memory (default) | code | both; envelope keys 'results' + 'code', kind=memory byte-shape-unchanged (no 'code' key)
code_get(projectId, hash) mirrors memory_get; unknown hash refused
One watch row serves both corpora — no digest-level classification; each ingestor self-filters by its own file-extension matcher

ai-raccoon.ignore: one file per watch/tree root, gitignore-subset syntax, filters BOTH pipelines (watch catch-up scans and memory_ingest_directory/memory_ingest_file); ignore wins over an explicit single-file ingest; editing the ignore file triggers a full re-scan
Overlapping watch containment: broader watch wins and prunes contained watches (one transaction); narrower-inside-broader is rejected naming the covering watch; equal-path re-add is idempotent

Repo-watch-by-default applies containment to every watch inside the registered root, then catch-up scans the whole repo; hidden directories and a built-in dependency-tree deny set are skipped for repo-root watches
Always-ingest: code files are chunked and stored pending even with no code engine configured; kind=code degrades to FTS5-only with a warning until an engine embeds them
model set code local activates a local code embedding engine; refuses any manifest whose declared dimensions are not 768
The code-reindex maintenance job drains pending code rows after a code engine change — configure-transaction invalidation, no model_migration outbox, no ToolGate interaction
Code lifecycle exclusions: no sync (DROP-stripped from every pushed snapshot), no sweep, no TTL, no promotion, no workspace scope — an explicit, re-derivable cache
search_quality exclusion: kind=code/both searches are never recorded (privacy — the table syncs); kind=memory recording is unchanged
out: Flipping the shipped default embedding model or chunker arm to the eval report's champion — an owner decision, never made by this feature

The full multi-repo evaluation corpus (2-3 vendored repos incl. a mandatory Python repo) — deferred pending owner approval of the specific repos (OQ5); only a small in-repo smoke eval-set ships with this feature
Tree-sitter AST chunking — v2 lever; v1 is line-range with brace-balance boundary preference
vec0 dimension reconcile for the code corpus — the D3 machinery is documented as an extension point, not exercised
codeRetrieval.* settings namespace — v1 reuses the existing RRF/fusion constants for the code section
Code chunk_index repair/backfill jobs — code is a re-derivable cache; loss costs a re-ingest, not a repair job

nonFunctional: Code is project-scoped only; no workspace or shared-tier code search (kind=code + scope=shared/workspace returns an empty code section, not an error)
Drain rate: the maintenance poll's default batch size is acceptable for incremental fingerprint-change re-embeds; a large-repo initial re-embed's wall time is a documented, not a hidden, cost
Non-interference: a code engine change never blocks a memory tool call; a code search's failure (unconfigured/unloadable engine) never affects a memory search in the same call
Privacy: code content and identifiers never leave the machine — no sync, no search_quality recording for code-adjacent queries
TDD mandatory: every scenario in code-corpus.feature is witnessed RED before the corresponding production code lands (plan §5, §6)
dotnet build + dotnet test green; existing memory retrieval gates unchanged by default (plan §5 regression guards)

targets.implementation: src/AiRaccoon.Core (CodeChunk, IgnoreRules, WatchOverlapResolver, code domain types) + src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure (CodeChunker, code schema/store, sync strip, code-reindex job) + src/AiRaccoon (CodeTools, MemoryTools kind param, model set code local CLI)
targets.tests: tests/AiRaccoon.Tests (scenario + unit + integration, per the WP1-WP8 catalog in docs/work/2026-08-21-code-search-moe-qa.md)

risks: Sync leakage is the highest-risk surface: a snapshot missing even one code-adjacent table (or its FTS5/vec0 shadow tables) leaks source content off-machine — gated on all three push call sites

Chunker quality without AST (line-range + brace-balance only) is unmeasured until the WP8 eval report lands; the token-window baseline arm and span-overlap scoring exist specifically to make this measurable, not to guarantee a result
A repo-watch-by-default without the hidden-dir/deny-set skip would index dependency trees (node_modules, .venv, etc.) at real embedding cost
The non-768 refusal is the ONLY protection for vec_code's fixed dimension — there is no post-hoc reconcile path for code the way there is for memory
